provider: azure pipelines build artifacts (as a free archive)

free_tier.stated: Pipeline artifacts are exempt from storage billing and follow the pipeline retention policy; a run marked retained indefinitely is not subject to that policy. The 2 GiB free allowance belongs to Azure Artifacts package feeds, a separate service.
free_tier.notes: the offer existed; the rejection records why it is unusable here

per_object_cap.stated: stated-absent: the Azure Pipelines retention and artifacts pages state no per-object size cap for pipeline artifacts.
per_object_cap.notes: not applicable: a rejected offer has no per-object cap to shard

retention.stated: Azure Pipelines: "No. The pipeline's retention policy and the maximum limits set by the administrator aren't applied when you mark an individual run or release to be retained indefinitely. It remains until you stop retaining it indefinitely."
retention.notes: Binding failure documented in record details.

egress.terms: stated-absent: the Azure Pipelines retention and artifacts pages state no egress or transfer-out price; they describe REST APIs to download artifacts.

interface_detail: Artifacts are published and downloaded through pipeline tasks and the Azure CLI (PublishPipelineArtifact, az pipelines runs artifact upload) and through REST APIs; they are not a general byte-store interface.
chaining: Azure Pipelines: "You can also use REST APIs to download run information and artifacts, and then store them in your own storage account or artifact repository." "Use Copy files instead of Publish build artifacts because data published as build artifacts is still subject to retention cleanup."
limits_note: the finding is the failure, not a constraint with a number
reliability_note: Deleting a pipeline run deletes all artifacts associated with that run; a run marked retained indefinitely is exempt from retention cleanup.
confidence_note: Rejection quoted from historical research records; unverified against live endpoints.
